report.verdict: Brightline's Customer Success Manager, Mid-Market role is a post-sale job, while your Vantage Fleet Software work points to new-business sales. Your sales results are strong, but I'd hesitate on this opening without retention or account ownership on the resume.
write_up: Brightline is looking for customer success experience, and your resume tells a different story: you moved from sales development into an Account Executive role at Vantage Fleet Software. The new-business results make your sales work worth a look, but they don't establish the post-sale work this job asks for.

The 25+ meetings line is a good model for the rest: it names the activity, its pace and who received the meetings. Your promotion is clear too. In the current role, a recruiter can see quota attainment and new business, but not the quota amount or the period behind the $1.4M.

Let's start with those two sales results. For Brightline, add any customer success, renewal, expansion or account-management work you've actually done, with the relevant numbers. Salesforce is already on your resume; keep it visible.

cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see you beat quota, but not what the target was. The amount gives that percentage a frame of reference.
cards.example: Achieved 132% of quota in FY2025 against a quota of [quota amount]
cards.question: What was your FY2025 quota?

cards.cannot_tell: The $1.4M is a real result, but a recruiter can't tell the period it covers or what a typical deal looked like. Both matter when comparing sales roles.
cards.example: Closed $1.4M in new business over [time period], with a typical deal size of [deal size]
cards.question: What period did the $1.4M cover, and what was your typical deal size?

cards.line: Booked 25+ meetings per month for the account executive team
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It gives the recruiter a concrete piece of work and a measure without making them guess who it was for.

fit.why: Your headline and current role both name Account Executive, and your recent work centers on closing new business.
fit.level: mid-level, promoted from Sales Development Representative to Account Executive
fit.note: Your full-cycle sales work, demos and Salesforce experience give you relevant ground to build on for Brightline. If you've supported customers after the sale, make that work visible without presenting sales results as retention results.

posting.summary: Brightline seeks a mid-market customer success manager to own accounts, renewals and expansion, with experience using customer data and working with executive sponsors.
missing: 3+ years in customer success or account management at a SaaS company
A track record of hitting retention or expansion targets, with numbers you can talk about
Comfortable with usage data: Gainsight, Salesforce, and a BI tool such as Looker
Experience running QBRs with VP-level sponsors
experience with analytics or data products
